title.narrative: CRTA: stöd till civilsamhället för att främja demokrati och EU-integrering
CRTA: support to CSOs to promote democracy and EU integration

description.narrative: Denna insats kommer skapa gynnsamma förutsättningar för och säkerställa utrymme för fortsatt utveckling och demokratisering genom stöd till kampanjer inom civilsamhället som berör huvudområdena i Serbiens EU-integrationsprocess: rättsväsende, demokratisk kultur och mediefrihet. Med hjälp av kommunikationsfärdigheter, kapacitet, kanaler och digitala verktyg kommer civilsamhället (organisationer och journalister) få möjligheten att engagera medborgare på mer effektivt sätt. Detta kommer också bidra till en förbättring av dialogen mellan medborgare och regeringen, samt återställa medborgarns tillit och tilltro till samhälleliga institutioner. Dessutom kommer en ökad medvetenhet om civilsamhällets insatser för stärkt demokratisering även leda till en större tillit till civilsamhällets roll som en viktig aktör för demokratisk utveckling.

This intervention will generate domestic force that will safeguard the space for further development and democratisation, by supporting civil society campaigns in areas of the primary importance for Serbia’s EU integrations: rule of law, democratic culture and media freedoms. Equipped with communication skills, capacities, channels and digital tools, civil society partners (CSOs, grassroots and journalists) will be able to engage citizens more deeply and reach their communication and advocacy goals more effectively. Civil society development will also ensure the adequate civic response in addressing gaps between citizens and governments, thus restoring the public confidence and trust in institutions. By raising awareness of civil society partners’ democratisation efforts, this intervention will help improve the general level of trust towards the civil society sector as generator of democratic development, and will raise citizens’ awareness of benefits of democratization and EU integration process.

The objectives of the intervention have not changed. The overall objective of the CRTA intervention is to support Serbia’s democratization in forging closer links with the EU through fostering pluralistic civil society, empowerment and strengthening the role of civil society actors as generators of democratic development. The activities aim to strengthen the objectives of the intervention by furthering its outreach and awareness raising efforts which in the first programme year proved to be of the utmost importance in raising the public attention to key challenges to the rule of law and mobilizing citizens around issues hampering the full exercise of their democratic rights. In this regard, CRTA intends to intensify its community building, citizen outreach and awareness raising initiatives and campaigns, while at the same time further strengthen its own capacities for public communication and citizen engagement. The Amendment to the initial agreement between the CRTA and Swedish Embassy in Belgrade was signed in December 2020, which extended the Cooperation Agreement for additional two years and added 12 million SEK to the total budget for continued activities until the end of 2022. Comprehensive communications capacity building support (training, technical and grant support) that CRTA provided in this period, has further raised the potential for broader influence and recognition of civil society on targeted issues in areas of the rule of law, democratic culture and media freedoms. Improvements of the approach within the third year of the Programme provided even more tailored-made and direct guidance and mentorship in development of impactful communications and outreach campaigns of supported partner organisations around issues pertaining the rule of law, democratic and media freedoms. These integrated communication and media campaigns, that are strategically, creatively and productively at a higher quality level, were designed to trigger citizen engagement, motivation and trust. This approach provided partner organisations with valuable opportunities to further strengthen communications, outreach and awareness raising capacities thus enabling the boost of their image and public support as democracy defenders.

- A total of 42 grants were provided to civil society organizations active in areas of the rule of law, democratic culture and media freedoms (ten grants in the first year, 14 in the second year, seven in the third year, four in the fourth year and seven in the fifth year).
- A total of 33 organisations from 17 local communities were provided with support in a five years period, with some of them being supported for several years under the programme. List of all organizations that were programme beneficiaries is listed in the Annex 1 at the end of the report.
- CRTA established the Communication Hub in order to serve as not only a central point for coordinating its own communication strategy and activities but also to provide support to its local civil society partners. The Hub activities related to support in strategic and crisis communication, campaigns, PR and media relations, digital communication and marketing, video production, design, web development etc.
- A total of 23 communication strategies (both overall and digital) was developed for 22 civil society organizations during this programme. In this way the CRTAs partners were equipped to effectively convey their message to the target audience, build trust and credibility, and foster engagement and participation. Moreover, a communication strategy helped them to manage their reputation and respond to crises effectively. In addition, a communication strategy enabled them to measure and evaluate the effectiveness of their communication efforts. Overall, the value of a communication strategy lies in its ability to guide organizations' communication efforts towards achieving their mission and goals effectively, building and maintaining trust and credibility, managing crises, and measuring and evaluating the effectiveness of their communication activities.
- CRTA supported through mentorship raising partners' capacities for public relations (PR) and media relations as they are crucial for organizations that seek to effectively communicate with their stakeholders and promote their message. During this programme, CRTA partners had been also capacitated for public speaking skills needed for effective sending of messages.
- Through the CRTA Training center and Communications Hub local civil society partners were provided with: 70 group and individual trainings; more than 25 long-term mentorship processes; 14 integrated media and outreach campaigns (including creative concepts design, digital and video production, media buying and placement, PR and media outreach, public events) for promoting and defending democracy, rule of law and media freedoms, which increased visibility of partner organisations and their work in different parts of Serbia, with some of them achieving the reach to around million online users.
- 10 online campaigns for promoting and defending democracy, rule of law and media freedoms that were created, produced and implemented; 23 communication strategies developed (both overall and digital); 14 websites and two video games developed; One documentary film produced; 82 promotional videos; nine media events; and three public opinion polls.
The programme worked importantly also to support CRTA organisational capacities, and particularly to strengthen own communications capacity. This is important for CRTA to broaden the base of supporters, as well as to enhance own influence for democracy promotion. Therefore CRTA worked under the programme to empower internal capabilities for the most effective public communication and outreach as well as for research. From 4% public recognition (in total population) in 2018 today every third person in Serbia (30%) in 2022 has heard of CRTA (and 94% of those who knows of CRTA perceive it as objective). CRTA and its members have become one of the main media interlocutors on topics concerning the state of democracy, rule of law, electoral process and media freedoms (in 2018 total of 1.345 media pieces about CRTA has been published in which 400 CRTA team members had been quoted while in 2022 CRTA has recorded a growth of 200% - total of 3.690 media pieces and 1.000 quotes of CRTA members), Due to digital communication and marketing capacity building CRTA succeeded in reaching new audiences through digital communication channels and multiple reach (e.g. Twitter community raised from 272 followers in 2018 to 21 thousand in 2022, Facebook approximately monthly reached 400 thousand and during media campaigns around 2 million).
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
